title: About
text:
Why This Matters
Language-learning apps often promote daily use, but the effectiveness of different study schedules is not always clear.
This project aims to provide a clearer, data-based perspective.

title: Results
text:
The schedules worked differently in practice.


The spaced group studied more frequently


The massed group logged more total study time



Because total study time was not perfectly balanced, the results should be interpreted as descriptive patterns, not a strict test of spacing alone.

title: Results
text:
XP Results
XP told two different stories.


Massed shows higher XP per session


Spaced shows higher XP per minute



XP reflects app activity, not language proficiency.

title: Results
text:
Weekly Engagement
Study behavior changed over time.

A good study routine needs to be sustainable, not just effective on a single day.

title: Results
section: How Study Style Affects Your Learning Experience？
text:
How Study Style Affects Your Learning Experience？


The spaced group consistently report a better overall learning experience than the massed group


Learners report higher concentration, confidence, enjoyment, and motivation, while also perceiving lower difficulty.

title: Results
text:
Test Results
Participants completed a Swedish proficiency test with four sections:

Grammar I

Grammar II

Vocabulary

Reading


Overall

Highest performance: Reading (57.2%)
Overall mean: 49.3%



By Group


The spaced group outperformed the massed group across all dimensions


The advantage was especially strong in vocabulary

title: Results
text:
Summary

Spaced learning showed a consistent advantage

The largest effect appeared in vocabulary

Results are descriptive, with individual differences


 Key Take Away:


Study frequency matters


Longer sessions produce more XP per session


XP is not the same as learning


Multiple metrics give a better picture


Short repeated practice may support vocabulary learning

title: Why Daily Practice Works Better
text:
Language-learning apps often encourage daily practice with streaks and reminders. But if two learners spend the same amount of time each week, does it matter how that time is distributed?
This project explores that question using an 8-week Duolingo learning study.

title: Why Daily Practice Works Better
text:
Language-learning apps often encourage daily practice with streaks and reminders. But if two learners spend the same amount of time each week, does it matter how that time is distributed?
This project explores that question using an 8-week Duolingo learning study.

title: Why Daily Practice Works Better
text:
Same Study Time, Different Routines
We compared two study schedules:

Spaced practice: 7 sessions × 10 minutes

Massed practice: 2 sessions × 35 minutes


Both groups aimed for 70 minutes per week, but distributed differently.

title: Why Daily Practice Works Better
section: What Do These Duolingo Terms Mean?
text:
What Do These Duolingo Terms Mean?
Session
A study period recorded in the learning log.
Lesson
A completed Duolingo activity.
XP
Experience points reflecting in-app activity.
Streak
Consecutive days of completing lessons.
Leaderboard
Ranking system based on XP.
